reasoning_trace: Read the full event stream in the injection window before checking the injector's own log. Payment 5c16d2fd completed the entire pipeline normally at 20:40:05.592, including a real SETTLEMENT_COMPLETE event from the settlement service -- so the system was healthy at the start of the window. One second later, an independent external witness (health_witness_monitor.py, which has zero knowledge of what was injected -- it only polls /actuator/health on a fixed schedule) logged HEALTH_CHECK_FAILED service=settlement consecutiveFailures=1 at 20:40:06.739. From that point forward, every subsequent payment (b7b91298, 01eb2807, 942821c0, 66b026c1, and others) shows the full upstream pipeline completing normally -- PAYMENT_SUBMITTED, PAYMENT_VALIDATED, AML_SCREENING_COMPLETE, RAIL_SELECTED, LIQUIDITY_RESERVED, PAYMENT_ROUTED -- and then simply stops. No SETTLEMENT_COMPLETE, no SETTLEMENT_FAILED, no settlement-service log line of any kind for these payments in the window. Two independent signals point the same direction: (1) the external witness explicitly names settlement as down, generated with no knowledge of the fault type or root service, and (2) the payment funnel itself shows a consistent stall exactly at the pipeline stage immediately after routing-execution, which is where settlement sits. No other service shows any anomaly in this window -- gateway, validation-enrichment, aml-compliance, routing-execution, fraud-scoring, and audit all continue logging normal completions for every payment throughout. Conclusion reached from evidence alone, before reading the injector's own log: settlement is the root cause.
confirmation_basis: Blind conclusion (settlement) matches the injector's own ground-truth log exactly. Independently corroborated by two separate evidence sources (external health-check witness + payment-funnel stall pattern), neither of which required foreknowledge of the answer.
